nodes.summary: Let $C_n = [-1, 1]^n$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$. If $C_n$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} C_n, \dots, v_q + \operatorname{int} C_n$ of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.
nodes.title: Covering the cube by translates of its interior needs $2^n$ translates

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$ equals the set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $|x_i| \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: The coordinate cube as an absolute-value box

nodes.summary: A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ lies in the interior of the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ if and only if $-1 < x_i < 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Interior of the coordinate cube

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is centrally symmetric: there is a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x$ lies in the cube if and only if $2c - x$ does.
nodes.title: The coordinate cube is centrally symmetric

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a convex body: it is compact and convex, and its interior in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: The coordinate cube is a convex body

nodes.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. There are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $C_3$ is contained in the union of the translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} C_3, \dots, v_8 + \operatorname{int} C_3$ of its interior.
nodes.title: Eight translates of the interior cover the three-dimensional cube

nodes.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Then $8$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $C_3$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} C_3$.
nodes.title: Eight is the least number of interior translates covering the three-dimensional cube

nodes.summary: Let $C_3 = [-1, 1]^3$ be the coordinate cube in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The translate covering number of $C_3$ by its interior $\operatorname{int} C_3$, the least number of translates of $\operatorname{int} C_3$ whose union contains $C_3$, equals $8$.
nodes.title: Translate covering number of the three-dimensional cube by its interior

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate cube is the set $[-1, 1]^n$ of points $x$ of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $-1 \le x_i \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Coordinate cube

nodes.summary: For every set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and every natural number $q$, $K$ has a cover by $q$ interior translates if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of the set $L = \operatorname{int} K$, the interior of $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: Interior-translate covers unfold to translate covers

nodes.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ interior translates, for a natural number $q$, when there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{q} (v_i + \operatorname{int} K)$, where $\operatorname{int} K$ is the interior of $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v + S = \{v + y : y \in S\}$.
nodes.title: Covering by interior translates

nodes.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ smaller positive homothets, for a natural number $q$, when there are real numbers $r_1, \dots, r_q$ with $0 < r_i < 1$ for every $i$ and vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every point of $K$ lies in $v_i + r_i K = \{v_i + r_i y : y \in K\}$ for some $i$.
nodes.title: Covering by smaller positive homothets

nodes.summary: For sets $K$ and $L$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a natural number $q$, $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of $L$ if and only if there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that every $x \in K$ lies in $v_i + L = \{v_i + y : y \in L\}$ for some $i$.
nodes.title: Pointwise form of covering by translates

nodes.summary: For sets $K$ and $L$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a natural number $q$, $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of $L$ when there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{q} (v_i + L)$, where $v + L = \{v + y : y \in L\}$.
nodes.title: Covering by translates

nodes.summary: If $q$ is a natural number such that every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is contained in the union of $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, then $8 \le q$.
nodes.title: Uniform interior-translate bounds in dimension three are at least eight

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a set and let $v, x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. The direction $v$ illuminates $x$ with respect to $K$ when $x$ lies on the boundary of $K$, $\|v\| = 1$, and $x + tv$ lies in the interior of $K$ for some real $t > 0$.
nodes.title: Illumination by a direction

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. Then some $q$ unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q$ illuminate $K$ if and only if some $q$ points $p_1, \dots, p_q$ outside $K$ illuminate $K$. Here the vectors illuminate $K$ when every boundary point $x$ of $K$ has an $i$ and a $t > 0$ with $x + t v_i$ in the interior of $K$, and the points illuminate $K$ when every boundary…
nodes.title: Directional and exterior-point illumination are equivalent

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the directional illumination number of $K$ equals its exterior-point illumination number. These are the least $q$ such that some $q$ unit vectors, respectively some $q$ points outside $K$, illuminate $K$, with the value $\infty$ when no finite family does.
nodes.title: Directional and exterior-point illumination numbers are equal

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. Then some $q$ unit vectors illuminate $K$ if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ homothets $v_1 + r_1 K, \dots, v_q + r_q K$ with $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $0 < r_i < 1$, repetitions allowed.
nodes.title: Directional illumination is equivalent to covering by smaller homothets

nodes.summary: The directional illumination number of a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $K$ is illuminated by $q$ directions, and $\infty$ if there is no such $q$.
nodes.title: Directional illumination number

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the directional illumination number of $K$ equals the least $q$ such that $K$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$. Both sides take the value $\infty$ when no finite family exists.
nodes.title: Directional illumination number equals the interior-translate covering number

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body and let $q$ be a natural number. Then some $q$ unit vectors illuminate $K$ if and only if $K$ is covered by $q$ translates $v_1 + \operatorname{int} K, \dots, v_q + \operatorname{int} K$ of its interior, repetitions allowed.
nodes.title: Directional illumination is equivalent to covering by interior translates

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a set and let $p, x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. The point $p$ illuminates $x$ with respect to $K$ when $p \notin K$, $x$ lies on the boundary of $K$, and $p + t(x - p)$ lies in the interior of $K$ for some real $t > 1$; that is, the ray from $p$ through $x$ meets the interior of $K$ at a point beyond $x$.
nodes.title: Illumination by an external point

nodes.summary: The external-point illumination number of a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that $K$ is illuminated by $q$ external points, and $\infty$ if there is no such $q$.
nodes.title: External-point illumination number

nodes.summary: If $q$ is the least natural number such that every convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, then the Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$ equals $q$.
nodes.title: A least uniform bound is the Hadwiger covering number

nodes.summary: The Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$, an element of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, is the least natural number $q$ such that every convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.
nodes.title: Hadwiger covering number

nodes.summary: The following statements are equivalent: for every $n \ge 1$, every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by at most $2^n$ homothets $v_i + r_i K$ with $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $0 < r_i < 1$; and for every $n \ge 1$, every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $2^n$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.
nodes.title: Two equivalent formulations of Hadwiger's covering conjecture

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ directions, for a natural number $q$, if there are unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (not necessarily distinct) such that for every boundary point $x$ of $K$ there are an index $i$ and a real $t > 0$ with $x + tv_i$ in the interior of $K$.
nodes.title: Illumination by $q$ directions

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ external points, for a natural number $q$, if there are points $p_1, \dots, p_q \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus K$ (not necessarily distinct) such that for every boundary point $x$ of $K$ there are an index $i$ and a real $t > 1$ with $p_i + t(x - p_i)$ in the interior of $K$.
nodes.title: Illumination by $q$ external points

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ there is a least natural number $q$ such that some $q$ unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q$ illuminate $K$: every boundary point $x$ of $K$ has an $i$ and a $t > 0$ with $x + t v_i$ in the interior of $K$.
nodes.title: Every convex body has a finite illumination number

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is an affine cube if $K = e([-1, 1]^n)$ for some affine bijection $e : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$, where $[-1, 1]^n$ is the coordinate cube $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : -1 \le x_i \le 1 \text{ for all } i\}$.
nodes.title: Affine cube

nodes.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is centrally symmetric when there is a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x \in K$ if and only if $2c - x \in K$.
nodes.title: Central symmetry about some center

nodes.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a convex body when it is compact and convex and its interior in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Convex bodies in Euclidean space

nodes.summary: The number $8$ is the least natural number $q$ such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed. Here $K$ is centrally symmetric when there is a point $c$ with $x \in K$ if and only if $2c - x \in K$.
nodes.title: Lassak's theorem for centrally symmetric bodies in dimension 3

nodes.summary: Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $16$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.
nodes.title: Papadoperakis's bound for Hadwiger's covering problem in dimension 3

nodes.summary: Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is covered by $14$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, repetitions allowed.
nodes.title: Prymak's bound for Hadwiger's covering problem in dimension 3

nodes.summary: If $q$ is the least natural number such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, then the symmetric Hadwiger covering number of dimension $n$ equals $q$.
nodes.title: A least uniform bound is the symmetric Hadwiger covering number

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the symmetric Hadwiger covering number in dimension $n$ is the least natural number $q$ such that every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior that is symmetric about some point) is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.
nodes.title: Symmetric Hadwiger covering number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $q$ be natural numbers. If every centrally symmetric convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior that is symmetric about some point) can be covered by $q$ not necessarily distinct translates of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.
nodes.title: Lower bound $2^n$ for centrally symmetric interior-translate covering

nodes.summary: Let $K, L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $q \in \mathbb{N}$. If $q$ is the least natural number $r$ such that $K$ is covered by $r$ translates of $L$, then the translate covering number of $K$ by $L$ equals $q$.
nodes.title: The translate covering number is the least covering count

nodes.summary: For sets $K, L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the translate covering number of $K$ by $L$ is the least natural number $q$ for which there are vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $K \subseteq (v_1 + L) \cup \dots \cup (v_q + L)$, and it is $\infty$ if no such $q$ exists.
nodes.title: Translate covering number

nodes.summary: For integers $n \ge 1$ and $q \ge 0$, every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) can be covered by $q$ translates of its interior if and only if every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ directions: there are unit vectors $v_1, \dots, v_q$ such that each boundary point $x$ of $K$ has some $i$ and some $t > 0$ with $x + t v_i$ in the interior of $K$.
nodes.title: Uniform covering by interior translates and uniform directional illumination

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $q$ be natural numbers. If every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) can be covered by $q$ not necessarily distinct translates of its interior, then $2^n \le q$.
nodes.title: Lower bound $2^n$ for uniform interior-translate covering

nodes.summary: For $n, q \in \mathbb{N}$, the uniform interior translate bound holds when every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) is covered by $q$ translates of its interior $\operatorname{int} K$, that is, $K \subseteq (v_1 + \operatorname{int} K) \cup \dots \cup (v_q + \operatorname{int} K)$ for some $v_1, \dots, v_q \in \mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: Uniform bound for covering convex bodies by interior translates

nodes.summary: For integers $n \ge 1$ and $q \ge 0$, every centrally symmetric convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior that is symmetric about some point) can be covered by $q$ translates of its interior if and only if every centrally symmetric convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is illuminated by $q$ external points: there are points $p_1, \dots, p_q$ outside $K$ such that each boundary point $x$…
nodes.title: Uniform covering of symmetric bodies and uniform illumination by external points

nodes.summary: For $n, q \in \mathbb{N}$, the uniform symmetric interior translate bound holds when every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) that is centrally symmetric, meaning that there is $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x \in K$ if and only if $2c - x \in K$, is covered by $q$ translates of its interior, that is,…
nodes.title: Uniform bound for covering centrally symmetric convex bodies by interior translates

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
